issues.body:
start_fuseki sets FUSEKI_PID=$! (line 171), but every call site invokes it in a command substitution to capture the ready-seconds — `JENA_READY_S="$(start_fuseki "$CORPUS" "$FUSEKI_PORT" ...)"` (line 264). That assignment happens in a subshell, so the parent's FUSEKI_PID stays "" for the whole run (verified empirically with a reduced repro: parent sees PID='', stop is a no-op, the child leaks).

The new code at line 323 depends on stop_fuseki actually working, and reuses the SAME port:
  stop_fuseki                                  # kills nothing
  start_fuseki "$FEATURE_CORPUS" "$FUSEKI_PORT" # cannot bind; port held by JVM #1

The second JVM fails to bind, but start_fuseki's readiness loop probes `ASK {}` at http://127.0.0.1:$FUSEKI_PORT/ds — which the STILL-RUNNING first server answers immediately. So start_fuseki returns 0 with ready_s ~= 0 and the `within10km_indexed` query is POSTed to the ORIGINAL direct-corpus dataset, whose spatial index holds 0 items (research/gap-geo-2026-07.md:276-281). The entire purpose of the change is defeated.

Two concrete consequences:
1. within10km_indexed returns 0 (or errors) forever -> count-disagree vs sparq's 51 -> timing withheld. Fail-safe on the number, but the feature never functions.
2. `indexed_variant_load_ready_s_advisory` records ~0s as the feature corpus's "load + spatial index" time for a corpus that was never loaded. That is a published, fabricated advisory figure.

The pre-existing variant of this bug (Geographica, line 646) is masked because it restarts on a DIFFERENT port (GG_FUSEKI_PORT = FUSEKI_PORT+1); it only leaks a competing JVM. This PR is the first caller for which the no-op is a correctness bug.
issues.fix_hint:
Publish the pid out of band so it survives the subshell — e.g. inside start_fuseki add `echo $! > "$TMP/fuseki.pid"` (or take a pid-file path as a 4th arg) and have stop_fuseki read+kill from that file, clearing it after; alternatively restructure start_fuseki to write ready-seconds to a file so it need not run in a command substitution at all.

Then harden against the masquerade that made the failure silent:
- After stop_fuseki, wait until the port is actually free (poll until the ASK probe FAILS, with a cap) before starting the replacement.
- Prefer a distinct port for the indexed leg (e.g. $((FUSEKI_PORT + 2)), avoiding GG_FUSEKI_PORT) and update ENDPOINT for that leg.
- Make readiness dataset-identifying, not just liveness: probe `ASK { ?f <http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql#hasGeometry> ?g }` for the feature leg so a stale direct-corpus server can never report ready. This is the check that would have turned this failure into an honest ERROR row instead of a bogus 0s advisory.
issues.title: stop_fuseki is a no-op (FUSEKI_PID lost to a command substitution), so the indexed leg silently runs against the old direct-corpus server on the same port

issues.body:
Every other pinned Jena rendering in this directory records the evidence that it actually executes and agrees. within10km.rq states: "verified count-equal to sparq's expected.tsv (51) on the pinned 100k corpus", and documents at length (sq-a8anf) that the previous standard rendering was NON-EXECUTABLE on jena 5.4.0 — a per-row UnitsConversionException that silently dropped every row and produced all-zero counts that were nearly trusted, forcing a retraction of the wave-1 nearest_k timings.

This new file carries no such evidence line, only a runtime oracle statement. Given the blocker above (the indexed leg has never been able to reach a feature-modelled dataset), nothing in this PR can have observed a real count from this query.

Two specific risk points:
1. UNITS. The file passes `10 "km"` — a plain string literal — whereas the verified sibling passes `10000 uom:metre` with PREFIX uom: <http://www.opengis.net/def/uom/OGC/1.0/>. Jena resolves the units argument through its units registry; if a bare label is not accepted the property function raises ExprEvalException and the workload becomes a permanent ERROR row. Using the same units form already proven to work on this jar removes the variable entirely.
2. LIMIT. spatial:withinCircle takes an optional trailing ?limit. It is omitted here, relying on Jena's default being unlimited. If the default is finite, the count silently caps.

Neither risk produces a false speed number (both degrade to ERROR or count-disagree), so this is major rather than blocker — but it means the workload may simply never yield a usable row.
issues.fix_hint:
After fixing the port/pid blocker, actually run the leg against the pinned jar and record the observed count in the file header in the same form the sibling uses, e.g. "verified count-equal to sparq's expected.tsv within10km (51) on the pinned 100k feature-modelled corpus, jena-fuseki-geosparql 5.4.0".

Switch the units argument to the already-proven URI form for consistency with within10km.rq:
  PREFIX uom: <http://www.opengis.net/def/uom/OGC/1.0/>
  ?e spatial:withinCircle (51 0 10000 uom:metre) .
(or uom:kilometre with radius 10). Pin the optional ?limit explicitly rather than depending on the default. Also confirm whether Jena indexes only the feature or both feature and geometry node for a hasGeometry pair — if both, the count is 102 not 51 and the rendering needs a `?e geo:hasGeometry ?g` guard.
issues.title: New Jena rendering is unverified and uses a bare "km" string for units instead of the uom: URI its verified sibling uses

issues.body:
Line 328:
  printf '%s\tERROR\tserver-not-ready\n' "$INDEX_WORKLOADS"

Every other producer of a row in this TSV iterates (`for wl in $INDEX_WORKLOADS`) and prints one row per workload. This one interpolates the whole space-separated variable as field 0. With a single element today it happens to be correct, so this is latent — but the moment a second indexed workload is added the error path writes one malformed row keyed "within10km_indexed <other>", and read_tsv (which keys on f[0]) then reports BOTH real workloads as "n/a" with no trace of the failure.

This sits specifically on the honest-ERROR-recording path, which is the one path that must not be silently wrong.
issues.fix_hint:
Loop, matching the surrounding style:
  for wl in $INDEX_WORKLOADS; do
    printf '%s\tERROR\tserver-not-ready\n' "$wl"
  done >> "$TMP/jena-geosparql.tsv"
issues.title: server-not-ready ERROR row prints the whole $INDEX_WORKLOADS list as one TSV field instead of looping

issues.body:
`JENA_STATUS="ok"` (line ~350) is reached unconditionally after the indexed block, including via the `start_fuseki` failure branch that logs "indexed-radius server not ready". The envelope then reports statuses["jena-geosparql"] = "ok" for a run in which half the Jena legs never started.

The per-row ERROR and the "n/a" advisory do keep the detail honest, and ingest-canonical-competitors.mjs only special-cases status === "failed", so nothing is actively misreported downstream. But the top-level status is the field a reader trusts for "did this engine run cleanly".
issues.fix_hint: Track partial failure, e.g. set JENA_STATUS="ok (indexed-variant leg not run: server not ready)" in the failure branch, or add a separate `jena_indexed_status` key to engines_meta alongside indexed_variant_load_ready_s_advisory.
issues.title: JENA_STATUS is set to "ok" even when the indexed-variant server failed to start

issues.body:
Two small reporting gaps:

1. The scale string reports only NPOINTS (from the direct corpus) and then says the variant "preserves the points with feature->geometry modelling". True for points, but the feature corpus has 2x the TRIPLES (one hasGeometry + one asWKT per entity). Since the indexed leg's load/index time is now recorded as an advisory, the reader needs the actual size of the dataset that time refers to.

2. The new `sparq_oracle_workload` field correctly documents that within10km_indexed's sparq column is borrowed from within10km — but ingest-canonical-competitors.mjs does not read it. It uses `cc.sparq` directly (lines ~225-231) as the row's `rows` column, so the published canonical table will show a `within10km_indexed` row with rows=51 and an empty sparq timing, with no indication the count came from a different workload. Nothing false is asserted, but the provenance the field was added to carry is lost at exactly the surface where it matters.
issues.fix_hint: Export FEATURE_NPOINTS="$(wc -l < "$FEATURE_CORPUS")" and include it in the scale string. For provenance, either mirror the note into count_crosscheck_note (which the ingester does propagate, line ~303) or teach the ingester to surface sparq_oracle_workload when it differs from the row key.
issues.title: Envelope scale string omits the feature corpus's triple count (2x) and the borrowed-oracle provenance is dropped by the ingester

issues.body:
The awk transform is correct against today's generator — I verified it against the exact format emitted by generate_corpus (crates/sparq-geo/examples/bench_geo.rs:86-97), including the fact that the WKT literal's internal space splits it across $3/$4 and that rebuilding the record via `$1 = geometry` with OFS=" " restores the original single-space separators byte-for-byte.

But that correctness rests on three unasserted assumptions: exactly one triple per line, the subject IS the entity, and single-space separators. If bench_geo gen ever emits a second triple per entity, changes spacing, or aligns output, the transform corrupts the corpus silently — the file is cached under /tmp/geo and reused, so the corruption would persist across runs. This also grows the /tmp/geo cache footprint that the header notes CI may key on.
issues.title: Feature transform has no post-condition guard against future corpus-shape drift

verdict.summary:
The intent is right and matches the recorded follow-up (research/gap-geo-2026-07.md:276-281 / sq-enfy3): Jena's spatial index holds 0 items on the direct `?e geo:asWKT` corpus, so giving it a feature->geometry variant is the correct way to let `spatial:withinCircle` use its index without touching the pinned corpus or its oracle. The awk transform in gen.sh is correct — I ran it against the exact output shape of `generate_corpus` (crates/sparq-geo/examples/bench_geo.rs:86) and it round-trips the WKT literal (whose internal space is split across $3/$4) byte-for-byte, emitting valid N-Triples. The oracle wiring (borrowing sparq's within10km count, omitting sparq_us for the Jena-only row) is honest and non-vacuous: a mismatch withholds the timing rather than publishing it.

But the new leg cannot work as written. `stop_fuseki` at geo-same-box.sh:323 is a guaranteed no-op, because `start_fuseki` assigns FUSEKI_PID inside a command substitution (line 264) and the parent never sees it — I reproduced this. The first Fuseki therefore keeps $FUSEKI_PORT; the second JVM cannot bind it, yet the readiness probe is answered by the still-running first server, so start_fuseki returns success with ready_s~0 and `within10km_indexed` executes against the OLD direct corpus (index = 0 items). Net effect: the feature is inert, and `indexed_variant_load_ready_s_advisory` publishes a fabricated ~0s "load + spatial index" figure for a corpus that was never loaded. The count oracle does contain the damage (51 vs 0 -> withheld), so no false speed number ships — but the advisory number is a real honesty defect.

Secondary: the new .rq carries no evidence it was ever executed (its verified sibling within10km.rq records "verified count-equal ... (51)"), and it passes units as the bare string "km" rather than the uom: URI that sibling uses — the exact class of unverified Jena rendering that produced the retracted wave-1 numbers in sq-a8anf.
